text: Writing clean code is a crucial skill for any developer. The primary goal is to make your code readable and easy to understand for others—and for your future self. Start by using clear naming conventions for your variables and functions; for example, `calculateTotal` is much better than `calc` or `x`. Break your logic down into small, focused functions that each do one thing. This not only simplifies testing but also improves maintainability, as you can easily find and fix issues without reading hundreds of lines. Remember, clean code is not about being clever; it is about being clear. Eventually, spending a little extra time writing clean code saves you hours of debugging later.
